test_title: SSC CPO 2024 Official Paper-I (Held On: 28 Jun, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution’.

This is the group of leaders __in whom the ruling government__ has placed its trust.
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"whom"** is used as the object of a verb or preposition. (जिसे)

 
 
• **Example: **The person whom you met yesterday is my friend.
 
 
 
• **"Whom" **is **correctly** used in the given sentence to indicate the object of the preposition "in". (जिसे)
 
 
• **Example: **This is the teacher in whom I have great confidence.
 
 
 
• Hence, the sentence is grammatically correct and does not need any substitution.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **No substitution.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Option 2: in who the ruling government** (जिसमें सत्तारूढ़ सरकार): Incorrect usage as "who" is not used as the object of a preposition.

 
 
• **Example:** Incorrect: This is the group of leaders in who the ruling government has placed its trust.
 
 
 
• **Option 3: with who the ruling government** (जिसके साथ सत्तारूढ़ सरकार): Incorrect preposition "with" changes the meaning of the sentence.
 
 
• **Example: **Incorrect: This is the group of leaders with who the ruling government has placed its trust.
 
 
 
• **Option 4: on who the ruling government** (जिस पर सत्तारूढ़ सरकार): Incorrect preposition "on" changes the meaning of the sentence.
 
 
• **Example:** Incorrect: This is the group of leaders on who the ruling government has placed its trust.
